description:
Set when a stream runs and arm it. Three parts: startAt, when the first session starts; end, when a session ends; repeat, what happens after it ends. The stream must already be startable — a destination plus either a playable video playlist or an attached published scene (check_stream_readiness) — otherwise the start time arrives and the start fails.
end is ONE of {at: time} or {afterSeconds: n} (counted from the moment the stream goes live); omit it for a session that runs until stopped.
repeat is ONE of:
- {calendar: {every: "DAY"}} or {calendar: {every: "WEEK", days: [...]}}: the next session starts at the same time of day, 24h or 7 days later, or on the listed weekdays. Needs end.at and a session shorter than 24h. `days` are UTC weekdays of the start instant, so a 9pm Monday Eastern session repeats on TUESDAY — the result echoes the committed window in UTC with its UTC weekday.
- {restart: {gapSeconds: n}}: the stream stops completely (the destination ends its broadcast, so YouTube or Twitch saves the recording), waits gapSeconds, and starts a new session, until it is stopped by hand or the schedule is cancelled. Needs end.afterSeconds. Going live takes a few minutes on top of the gap.
Example, 11 hours on air then a 10 minute break, forever: {startAt, end: {afterSeconds: 39600}, repeat: {restart: {gapSeconds: 600}}}. Omit repeat to run once.
Replaces any existing schedule; cancel_stream_schedule disarms it. end.afterSeconds also becomes the stream's streamDuration. Returns the stream (with `schedule` in this same shape) and committedWindow: the start (and end.at) in UTC, the UTC start weekday, and the times as you sent them.

end.description: When a session ends: exactly one of at or afterSeconds. Omit for a session that runs until stopped.

afterSeconds.description: The session ends this many seconds after the stream goes live, e.g. 39600 for 11 hours.

at.description: The session ends at this moment. An instant in the user's own time zone, with that zone's offset: 6am US Eastern daylight time is 2026-09-22T06:00:00-04:00. The user's clock numbers are not UTC.

repeat.description: What happens after a session ends: exactly one of calendar or restart. Omit to run once.

calendar.description: Repeat at the same time of day. Needs end.at and a session shorter than 24h.

days.description: Only with every=WEEK: the UTC weekdays a session starts on (distinct). Omit for the same UTC weekday as startAt.

every.description: DAY: every 24h. WEEK: every 7 days, or on `days`.

restart.description: Stop, wait, start a new session, repeatedly. Needs end.afterSeconds.

gapSeconds.description: Seconds between the end of one session and the scheduled start of the next, e.g. 600; 0 restarts at once.

startAt.description: When the first session starts; must be in the future. An instant in the user's own time zone, with that zone's offset: 6am US Eastern daylight time is 2026-09-22T06:00:00-04:00. The user's clock numbers are not UTC.

name: schedule_stream

committedWindow.description: The committed window restated in UTC, to check the time zone was read as meant.

asRequested.description: startAt, endAt and offset exactly as sent.

endAtUTC.description: end.at in UTC; null when the end is a duration or there is none.

startWeekdayUTC.description: UTC weekday of the start: the day a weekly repeat runs on.

end.description: When the session ends: one of at or afterSeconds is set. Null: it runs until stopped.

repeat.description: What happens after the session ends: one of calendar or restart is set. Null: it runs once.

startAt.description: When the session starts, or started.

schedule.description: The stream's schedule, in the shape schedule_stream takes; null when nothing is scheduled.

code.description: Stable — branch on it: INVALID_INPUT, REVISION_REQUIRED, STALE_PUBLISH, CONFIRM_REQUIRED, UNAVAILABLE, …

currentRevision.description: CONFLICT: the revision it has now

detail.description: What is wrong, in a sentence

errors.description: Each problem, when a check refused it

title: Schedule stream
